notes: Departments sourced from each government's official portal (punjab.gov.in/departments, haryana.gov.in/departments, chandigarh.gov.in/other-departments) as of 2026-09-25. GAP: the base state file for Punjab/Haryana/Chandigarh (st-pb-government / st-hr-government / st-ch-government, Governor/Administrator, Chief Minister, ministers, Chief Secretary, DGP) does NOT yet exist anywhere in data/raw/*.json as of this write (only district/local-government-tier entities for st-pb/st-hr/st-ch exist, in local-lgd.json) — confirmed by grep across all raw files for 'st-pb-pos-', 'st-hr-pos-', 'st-ch-pos-' and for the current CMs' names (Bhagwant Mann, Nayab Singh Saini), all of which returned nothing. Per the task's own instruction to reference minister IDs rather than redefine them, and the schema's 'never invent an ID' quality bar, headPositionId (minister -> department) was deliberately left OMITTED on every department entity here, and no 'heads' relations were written, rather than guess at st-pb-pos-minister-<n> / st-hr-pos-minister-<n> numbering that a future states-pb-hr-ch segment might not match. Likewise no 'oversees' relation from a Chief Secretary position was written (st-pb/hr/ch-pos-chief-secretary do not exist yet either), consistent with the task's own conditional on that relation. Ministerial portfolios for Punjab and Haryana ARE visible in the department-name text below via each department's assigned Administrative Secretary's official title where sourced from a live posting page, but the elected-minister layer itself is a prerequisite this segment does not own. RECOMMENDATION: once a states-pb-hr-ch(-r2) base segment lands with real st-pb-pos-minister-<n>/st-hr-pos-minister-<n>/st-pb-pos-chief-secretary/st-hr-pos-chief-secretary/st-ch-pos-administrator IDs, a follow-up pass should backfill headPositionId on these department entities and add the 'heads'/'oversees' relations — the department-to-minister-portfolio mapping is recoverable from the same official sources cited in each department's `sources`. sector: used 'federal' (not the task brief's literal 'executive') to match SCHEMA.md ('federal' = States/UTs and everything inside them) and the existing precedent in data/raw/states-ka-ap-tg.json, which already uses 'federal' for its state_department entities (Karnataka/AP/Telangana police) — using 'executive' would misplace ~140 entities into the Union-executive wedge of the radial layout. Chandigarh has no elected Council of Ministers (it is a UT with no legislature, administered by the Punjab Governor as Administrator via an IAS Adviser/Secretariat); its department entries reference 'st-ch-pos-administrator' as appointedBy on secretary positions (SCHEMA's own canonical ID for a UT Administrator) rather than any minister position, which does not exist for Chandigarh even in concept. Chandigarh's autonomous institutions (PGIMER, CITCO, Chandigarh Housing Board, government colleges), the Municipal Corporation, and quasi-judicial bodies (State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Police Complaints Authority, State Election Commission) were excluded from this department list — they are not 'state_department' kind and belong to other segments/kinds. Secretary coverage: Punjab 48/52 departments (from the live punjab.gov.in/government/whos-who/admin-secretaries page, which gives full name + IAS batch + current portfolio for every officer; 4 depts — Employment Generation/Skill Development & Training, Information & Public Relation, Program Implementation — had no officer explicitly named against them on that page and were left without adminHeadPositionId per the 'omit rather than guess' instruction). Haryana 14/47 (haryanacmoffice.gov.in/administrative-secretaries only renders Chief Secretary + the 8 Additional Chief Secretaries in static HTML — the fuller Principal Secretary/Secretary tier appears to be client-rendered and was not retrievable via curl within this run's WebSearch budget, which was already exhausted by earlier sibling research segments in this session; the linked PDF of admin-secretary emails at cswww.haryana.gov.in did not resolve). Chandigarh 35/39 (from the chandigarh.gov.in/whos-who directory, which is unusually complete: Secretary-level for most, Joint-Secretary-level used only for Technical Education where no Secretary-rank officer was named). All secretary `since` dates omitted — none of the three source pages publish a posting date, only the current officer's name/batch/portfolio; per schema, guessing a date was avoided.

One of the 4 'no officer named' departments was wrong: Department of Revenue, Rehabilitation & Disaster Management does have a sourced ACS (Anurag Verma) on the live page and has been added.
